gloss: bad omen; ill omen; unlucky sign

definitions.gloss: bad omen; ill omen; unlucky sign
definitions.explanation: A sign or event believed to foretell misfortune or disaster. Used both literally in contexts involving superstition and figuratively to describe worrying signs.

examples.japanese: カラスが{鳴|な}くのは{凶兆|きょうちょう}だという。
examples.english: They say a crow cawing is a bad omen.

examples.japanese: {不吉|ふきつ}な{夢|ゆめ}を{凶兆|きょうちょう}と{受|う}け{止|と}めた。
examples.english: I took the ominous dream as a bad omen.

examples.japanese: {株価|かぶか}の{急落|きゅうらく}は{経済|けいざい}{危機|きき}の{凶兆|きょうちょう}かもしれない。
examples.english: The sharp drop in stock prices may be an omen of an economic crisis.

notes:
A somewhat literary or dramatic word for a bad omen. Appears in novels, news commentary, and discussions of superstitions. The opposite is {吉兆|きっちょう} (good omen).

FORMS:
{凶|きょう} (bad luck, misfortune) + {兆|ちょう} (sign, omen)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {凶兆|きょうちょう}と{見|み}なす: to regard as a bad omen
- {凶兆|きょうちょう}を{感|かん}じる: to sense a bad omen
- {凶兆|きょうちょう}が{現|あらわ}れる: a bad omen appears

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {不吉|ふきつ}: unlucky, ominous — an adjective describing the quality, while {凶兆|きょうちょう} is the sign itself
- {吉兆|きっちょう}: good omen — the direct antonym
- {前兆|ぜんちょう}: omen, harbinger — neutral (can be good or bad)
- {悪|わる}い{予感|よかん}: bad premonition — more colloquial and personal
